record.paper_title: Open problems in theory of metric linear spaces
record.original_question: Let X be a non-locally convex F-space. Does X contain a subspace M such that the quotient space X/M has no nontrivial continuous linear functionals?

evidence.quote: PROBLEM l6 • - Let X be a non-locally convex space. Does X contain a subspace such that there is no nontrivial linear continuous functionals in the quotient space ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An F-space is a topological vector space whose topology is induced by a complete translation-invariant metric. Such a space X is said to be locally convex if it has a base of neighborhoods of 0 consisting of convex sets; otherwise it is called non-locally convex. A continuous linear functional on a topological vector space Y is called nontrivial if it is not identically zero.

Question: Let X be a non-locally convex F-space. Does there always exist a closed linear subspace M ⊆ X such that the quotient F-space X/M admits no nontrivial continuous linear functional?
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not return a definitive resolution of this question. Foundational results in the area (notably by Kalton, Peck and Roberts) establish the existence of specific non-locally convex F-spaces with trivial dual (e.g., L_p[0,1] for 0<p<1), but no source found confirms or refutes the general statement that every non-locally convex F-space has a closed subspace whose quotient has trivial dual. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: An F-space Sampler — Kalton, Peck, Roberts
status_evidence.snippet: Monograph on the theory of non-locally convex F-spaces and their duals.
status_evidence.claim: Standard reference for problems about duals/quotients of non-locally convex F-spaces; does not record an affirmative general solution to this question.

status_evidence.title: L_p-spaces for 0<p<1 (K. Conrad)
status_evidence.snippet: L_p[0,1] for 0<p<1 has only the zero continuous linear functional.
status_evidence.claim: Illustrates the existence of non-locally convex F-spaces with trivial dual, but does not address the quotient question for arbitrary non-locally convex F-spaces.
